newsitem.title: UK: S&P ups Glaxo Wellcome long term to AA.
newsitem.headline: S&P ups Glaxo Wellcome long term to AA.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it raised Glaxo Wellcome's long term rating to AA from AA minus, and said the outlook was stable.
S&P also said it affirmed Glaxo Wellcome's A1 plus commercial paper ratings.

"The upgrade acknowledges various positive developments following Glaxo's early 1995 acquisition of Wellcome for 9.3 billion stg," S&P said in a statement. "The acquisition has made Glaxo Wellcome the largest pharmaceuticals group in the world with a market share of about 5 percent."
The rating agency said regulatory approvals in various countries for important drugs give further evidence of the strength of the company's rich research and development pipeline.
Glaxo Wellcome's restructuring programme is well on track, S&P said, and on completion the combined group should be better placed to meet the structural changes facing the pharmaceutical industry.

S&P said Wellcome, like Glaxo, has been dependent on one drug with limited remianing patent protection in the U.S. for a large proportion of its sales. The patent for Zovirax, a herpes treatment, expires in 1997.
"Zantac, the world's largest selling prescription medicine in 1995, increasingly faces a multitude of challenges such as generic competition and new treatments," S&P said.

S&P said the inevitable decline of Zantac following its U.S. patent expiry in July 1997 could lead to about two years of low sales growth for the group as a whole. Subsequently, the rating agency said the company should resume well above industry average growth again.
Exlcuding Zantac, the group grew 14 percent in the first half of 1996, S&P said.
